## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One project-policy fix is needed: the new `--exclude` flag does not read its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, which the CLI flag policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. Apart from that, the exclusion logic and its tests are consistent for basename glob matching.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to `cli/main.py`. `collect()` uses the flag to skip files whose basename matches any pattern and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests in `tests/test_main.py`, and adds the fixture `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the `--exclude` default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — Setting `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` has no effect, because the flag is declared with `default=[]` and nothing reads the environment. This breaks `.agents/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that pass options through the environment cannot exclude files, so unwanted files still end up in their archives. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choosing and documenting a separator for multiple globs, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
